classification.difficultyReason: Requires interpreting bearings, applying the sine rule, finding the perpendicular distance to a road and transferring that distance to an elevation triangle.

inlines.text: Use the sine rule in the horizontal triangle, then find the perpendicular distance to the road and apply the elevation angle.

answer.worked:
Let $P$ and $O$ be Mary's starting and final positions, $M$ the mountain's base, $A$ the closest point on the road and $H$ the summit. The reverse bearing from $O$ to $P$ is $135^\circ$.

$$\begin{align*}\angle MPO&=335^\circ-315^\circ=20^\circ\\\angle POM&=135^\circ-105^\circ=30^\circ\\\angle PMO&=180^\circ-20^\circ-30^\circ=130^\circ\end{align*}$$

Apply the sine rule in $\triangle POM$:

$$\begin{align*}\frac{PM}{\sin30^\circ}&=\frac{142}{\sin130^\circ}\\PM&=\frac{142\sin30^\circ}{\sin130^\circ}\end{align*}$$

Since $AM$ is perpendicular to the road, $\triangle PAM$ is right-angled. Using the unrounded value of $PM$,

$$\begin{align*}AM&=\frac{142\sin30^\circ}{\sin130^\circ}\sin20^\circ\end{align*}$$

In right-angled $\triangle AMH$,

$$\begin{align*}\tan8^\circ&=\frac{MH}{AM}\\MH&=\frac{142\sin30^\circ\sin20^\circ}{\sin130^\circ}\tan8^\circ\\MH&\approx4.455\text{ km}\end{align*}$$
